summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, diastolic heart failure, and a history of drug-resistant UTIs was admitted for pyelonephritis and hyperglycemia. She presented with left flank pain, dysuria, and a blood glucose over 500. Urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae resistant to multiple antibiotics, prompting a switch from Zosyn to meropenem. A PICC line was placed to complete a 14-day course of IV antibiotics at home. Her insulin regimen was optimized with an increase in morning NPH to 30 units and a revised sliding scale to prevent hypoglycemia. She was discharged home with services for IV antibiotic administration and daily straight catheterization to prevent urinary retention and recurrent infections.
